name: Baron Aquanis
summary: Blackfathom Deeps is where the Twilight's Hammer has made its lair, and Baron Aquanis rises from its flooded Moonshrine Ruins. He appears when someone disturbs the Fathom Stone, while the Earthen Ring suspects the cult has corrupted him.

sections.title: Guardian of the Fathom Stone
sections.body: The Fathom Stone lies beneath the flooded halls of the Moonshrine Ruins, right under the noses of the Twilight's Hammer cultists who occupy them. Within the stone rests a fathom core, a device that reveals the history of nearby elemental activity when properly read. Je'neu Sancrea of the Earthen Ring sends Horde adventurers to recover it. Disturbing the stone draws Baron Aquanis up from the depths.

sections.title: Corruption of the Depths
sections.body: The Earthen Ring has long considered Baron Aquanis a corrupted elemental power. When he is destroyed, he leaves behind a Strange Water Globe, an impervious orb filled with putrid, sloshing water that seems to have fed him energy. Je'neu Sancrea believes the globe may prove what corrupted the baron and how. He would not be surprised if the Twilight's Hammer were responsible.

faq.q: Where can I find Baron Aquanis?
faq.answer: Baron Aquanis dwells in the flooded Moonshrine Ruins deep inside Blackfathom Deeps. He rises from the water when someone disturbs the underwater Fathom Stone, as Horde adventurers do while recovering its fathom core for Je'neu Sancrea.

faq.q: What is the Strange Water Globe?
aliases: what is the water globe for
faq.answer: The Strange Water Globe is what Baron Aquanis leaves behind when he is destroyed. The impervious orb holds putrid, sloshing water that seems to have fed his elemental energy. Je'neu Sancrea of the Earthen Ring wants to study it for proof of what corrupted the baron and how.

faq.q: Why is the Earthen Ring interested in Baron Aquanis?
faq.answer: The Earthen Ring watches over the balance of the elements. Je'neu Sancrea and his comrades have long considered Baron Aquanis a corrupted elemental power. With the Twilight's Hammer in the Moonshrine Ruins, they fear the cult may be coercing the elements to work against the Horde. The baron's remains and the fathom core could show what the cult is doing.

The fathom core is an elemental artifact housed within the sunken Fathom Stone. Properly read by a trained shaman, it reveals a comprehensive history of regional elemental activity and can expose whatever dark rituals the Twilight's Hammer is conducting in the ruins.

faq.q: Is Baron Aquanis allied with the Twilight's Hammer?
faq.answer: As far as anyone can tell, Baron Aquanis is a corrupted elemental rather than a willing servant. The Twilight's Hammer cultists occupying the Moonshrine Ruins are the obvious suspects. Je'neu Sancrea says their involvement would not surprise him, but he wants proof before saying for sure.

faq.q: Does the Alliance have business with Baron Aquanis?
faq.answer: Not directly. The Fathom Stone and Baron Aquanis are Je'neu Sancrea's concern. He is an Earthen Ring shaman working with the Horde on Ashenvale's coast, and he sends Horde adventurers to recover the fathom core. Alliance explorers in Blackfathom Deeps have other errands there.

angles.text: For shamans of the Earthen Ring, Baron Aquanis is a tragic example of elemental perversion. His tainted remains offer insight into purifying twisted spirits.
Je'neu Sancrea works with the Horde on Ashenvale's coast. The fathom core his Horde helpers recover is meant to show what the Twilight's Hammer is doing to the elements there.
